practice.solution: Real-future conditional → if + **apologises**; the main clause keeps *will withdraw*. 'Would apologise' belongs to the unreal frame and breaks the pair.
practice.shortcut: if + present, will + verb.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

If I **was** the district collector, I would widen the storm-water drains first.
practice.solution: Unreal present (I am not the collector) → **were** for all persons: if I **were** the collector. 'Had been' would demand 'would have widened' in the main clause.
practice.shortcut: unreal present → if I were.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

My father **is working** in the same mill for twenty-two years.
practice.solution: *For twenty-two years* + still employed → **has been working**. The plain continuous drops the 'still going' meaning; the past perfect continuous breaks the link with now.
practice.shortcut: for + length + continuing → has been -ing.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The two families **know** each other since 1998.
practice.solution: *Since 1998* + still true → **have known**. 'Knew' detaches the fact from the present; 'are knowing' is not a stative use.
practice.shortcut: since + point + state → present perfect.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The bundle of old files **were** sent to the record room.
practice.solution: The subject is **bundle**; 'of old files' is an interrupter → the bundle **was** sent. The other plural helpers repeat the illusion.
practice.shortcut: cover the 'of' phrase; bundle is singular.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The captain, as well as the openers, **were** blamed for the collapse.
practice.solution: 'As well as' adds information; it never makes the subject plural → the captain **was** blamed. The plural helpers all follow the added noun instead of the true subject.
practice.shortcut: as well as / along with → verb follows the first noun.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The list of holidays **have been** announced by the district administration.
practice.solution: The subject is **list** (singular) → the list **has been** announced. 'Were' and 'are been' repeat the plural fault; 'are been' is not even a form.
practice.shortcut: the list has — not have.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Each of the shortlisted candidates **are** to report by nine tomorrow.
practice.solution: **Each** is unconditionally singular → each **is** to report. The plural *candidates* inside the 'of' phrase cannot change the opener.
practice.shortcut: each of → singular.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

One of my cousins **have settled** in Wellington.
practice.solution: The subject is **one** → one **has settled**. 'Have settle' keeps the plural helper and drops the participle; the original agrees with the decoy noun *cousins*.
practice.shortcut: one of + plural noun + singular verb.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Either the secretary or the joint secretaries **is** responsible for the circular.
practice.solution: With either…or, the verb agrees with the **nearer** subject — *the joint secretaries* (plural) → **are** responsible. 'Is' and 'was' follow the distant 'secretary'.
practice.shortcut: either…or → nearer subject.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Not only the students but also the wardens **was** honoured at the function.
practice.solution: The nearness rule applies to not only…but also too: the nearer subject *the wardens* is plural → **were** honoured. 'Has been' would also break the passive plural.
practice.shortcut: not only…but also → nearer subject.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

A number of films **has been** censored this month.
practice.solution: **A number of** means 'many' → plural: a number of films **have been** censored this month. ('The number of films has…' would be the singular frame.)
practice.shortcut: a number of → plural verb.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Many a farmer **have** shifted to drip irrigation in the drought belt.
practice.solution: **Many a + singular noun** is grammatically singular despite the plural meaning → many a farmer **has** shifted. The plural helpers follow the meaning, not the grammar.
practice.shortcut: many a → singular, always.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The second model is **far more better** than the first.
practice.solution: **Better** is already comparative → drop the doubled marker: **far better** than the first. 'More good' re-doubles; 'best' breaks the two-item frame announced by *than the first*.
practice.shortcut: cut the doubled marker; keep the intensifier.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Of all the vaccines, this one is **the more effective**.
practice.solution: **Of all** the vaccines announces more than two → superlative: **the most effective**. 'The more effective' fits only a two-item frame; 'effective most' is not a form.
practice.shortcut: of all → superlative; of the two → comparative.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The streets of Mysuru are cleaner than **Bangalore**.
practice.solution: Compare streets with streets → **those of Bangalore** (plural *those* for plural *streets*). 'That of' is singular; 'Bangalore's streets' doubles the clause.
practice.shortcut: plural noun compared → those of.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The proteins in millets are higher than **most cereals**.
practice.solution: Proteins must be compared with proteins → **those of most cereals** (plural). 'That of' is singular; the original compares proteins with cereals — unlike things.
practice.shortcut: name both sides of the comparison before choosing.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The floors of the new hostel are cleaner than **the old hostel**.
practice.solution: Floors with floors → **those of the old hostel**. 'That of' is singular; 'the old hostel's floors are' produces a doubled clause.
practice.shortcut: floors (plural) → those of.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The Goods and Services Tax is **preferable than** the older levy system.
practice.solution: **Preferable** takes **to**, never than → preferable **to** the older levy system. 'More preferable than' doubles the comparison; 'prefer to' changes the word class.
practice.shortcut: preferable / superior / senior → to.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

My sister **prefers coffee than** tea in winter.
practice.solution: **Prefer X to Y**: prefers coffee **to** tea. The original's subject is third person singular, so *prefers* with the -s must stay — only the partner word changes.
practice.shortcut: prefer → to; keep the subject-verb agreement.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Mumbai is the **larger** of the two megacities in terms of population.
practice.solution: **Of the two** → comparative: the **larger** of the two megacities is exactly right → No substitution required. 'Largest' needs three or more; 'more larger' doubles the marker.
practice.shortcut: of the two → the …er of.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Iron is **the most useful** of the two metals for construction.
practice.solution: **Of the two** metals → comparative: **the more useful**. 'The most useful' claims three or more; 'more useful' drops the required *the*.
practice.shortcut: count the items before choosing the degree.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The child is very fond **of** his grandmother.
practice.solution: The fixed pair is **fond of** → the original is standard → No substitution required. 'Fond for', 'fond with' and 'fond at' are not English.
practice.shortcut: fond of — learn the pair; do not repair a correct sentence.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The committee does not approve **for** the proposal.
practice.solution: The fixed pair is approve **of** → does not approve **of the proposal**. 'Agree with/to' tempts by meaning, but the verb here is *approve*.
practice.shortcut: approve of; agree with a person / to a plan.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

He returned after **an hour** with the medicine.
practice.solution: **Hour** begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent) → **an hour** is correct → No substitution required. 'A hour' follows the spelling instead of the sound.
practice.shortcut: an hour, an honest — silent h.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The temple was built near **a ancient** trading route.
practice.solution: **Ancient** begins with a vowel sound → **an ancient** trading route. Only the article needs repair; the smallest change wins.
practice.shortcut: a/an by sound: ancient → an.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Please **revert back** to my mail by Friday.
practice.solution: **Revert** already means 'come back' → the echo *back* is redundant: 'please **revert to** my mail'. 'Reverting to' breaks the request form; the original keeps the echo.
practice.shortcut: revert, return, repeat — cut the echo word.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

He **wrote back a reply** immediately after reading the notice.
practice.solution: **Wrote a reply** — 'back' echoes the idea already inside *reply* → the clean form is 'wrote a reply immediately'. 'Had wrote' uses the wrong participle.
practice.shortcut: one idea, one word; wrote = put in writing.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The doctor's **advise** was to rest for a week.
practice.solution: The slot is a noun (the subject of 'was') → the doctor's **advice**. *Advise* is the verb; 'advising' would wreck the structure.
practice.shortcut: advice = noun; advise = verb.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The new rule will **affect** every contract worker.
practice.solution: The slot needs the verb 'to influence' → **affect** is correct → No substitution required. *Effect* is the noun; 'effect on' turns the verb slot into a noun phrase.
practice.shortcut: affect = verb; effect = noun.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

No sooner **did the inspector leave** than the clerks started chatting.
practice.solution: 'No sooner **did the inspector leave** than…' satisfies the full frame: inversion (did + subject + base) with the partner *than* → No substitution required. 'The inspector had left' and 'the inspector left' drop the inversion; 'did the inspector left' pairs *did* with a past form.
practice.shortcut: no sooner did + base…than — check all three parts before repairing.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Hardly **the results had been announced** when the servers crashed.
practice.solution: Fronted **Hardly** demands inversion: hardly **had the results been announced** when…. The original keeps statement order; 'the results had announce' breaks the participle and the order.
practice.shortcut: hardly + had + subject + been + participle…when.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

No sooner **the train had left** the platform than the TTE began checking tickets.
practice.solution: **No sooner** demands helper-first order: no sooner **had the train left** than…. The original hides the helper after the subject; 'the train left' loses both the inversion and the perfect; 'had leave' breaks the participle.
practice.shortcut: no sooner + had + subject + participle…than.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Seldom **we see** such discipline in a government office.
practice.solution: Fronted **Seldom** forces inversion with do-support: seldom **do we see** such discipline. The other options keep statement order and only shuffle tense.
practice.shortcut: seldom / never / rarely at the front → do/did or helper first.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Never **I have** witnessed such a peaceful poll in this constituency.
practice.solution: Fronted **Never** pulls the helper before the subject: never **have I witnessed**. The tense stays present perfect — only the order changes; 'I have witness' breaks the participle.
practice.shortcut: never + helper + subject + participle.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

**Being a rainy day**, the mela was cancelled by the committee.
practice.solution: The mela cannot *be* a rainy day — the opener dangles. The absolute construction gives it its own subject: **It being a rainy day**, the mela was cancelled.
practice.shortcut: -ing opener without a doer → It being…

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Having eaten our lunch, **the train** departed from platform three.
practice.solution: Who ate the lunch? Not the train. The doer must head the main clause: **we boarded the train**. 'The train was departed' is not English in this sense and still dangles.
practice.shortcut: -ing opener borrows the main subject — name the doer.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The training module covers **typing, to file papers, and how to draft mails**.
options: typing, filing papers, and drafting mails
typing, filing papers, and to draft mails
typing, to file papers and draft mails
practice.solution: Every item after *covers* must share one shape → the uniform -ing list: **typing, filing papers, and drafting mails**. The options that keep a to-item or a how-to clause leave the line broken.
practice.shortcut: lists stay parallel: match the first item's shape.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

She is **not only intelligent but also she works hard**.
options: not only intelligent but also hardworking
not only intelligent but works hard also
not only an intelligent but also hard work
practice.solution: The correlative must join equal shapes: **not only intelligent but also hardworking** — two adjectives. The original pairs an adjective with a full clause; the decoys break the pair order or the word class.
practice.shortcut: not only X but also Y — X and Y must be the same kind.
